title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon: GDM's Opus/Sol Contender
summary:
Google DeepMind shipped Gemini 4 Neon , its fourth Gemini 4 model in about seven weeks. If you’re confused about the naming, you’re not alone; the 1.5 month old Argon is now retired , the old Pro and Flash from Gemini 1-3 are dead, and if you’re thinking the names are based on atomic weights, Neon (10), the midtier model is faster/cheaper than Carbon (6). This is a helpful guide to the current leading models and sizes: 

 Because of how distillation, RL, and benchmarking works, Neon technically outperforms Carbon by some measures despite being a smaller model… 

 Also today, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share , above its initial range, and Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute in a $4.5B all-stock deal . Anthropic · Palo Alto Networks 

 AI News for November 17–18, 2026. We checked 12 subreddits and 544 Twitter accounts . Browse past issues .

 Pricing and specs. Neon costs $3 for input, $0.15 for cached input and $15 for output per million tokens. It has a 1M-token context window and four effort levels. Vals reports a maximum output limit of 1M tokens. Google · Vals

title: llm-gemini 0.38
summary:
Release: llm-gemini 0.38 

 Today Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon . I wrote recently about how confusing the pricing for the Gemini 4 series was - Neon has somehow made this even worse.

 Previously the Gemini 4 lineup was Hydrogen, Argon, and Carbon - where Argon and Carbon were the same price , and Hydrogen was 3/4 of that price now but will be 1/4 of that price when the other two double an 1st December once their initial discount pricing expires.

 The Neon announcement pretends that Argon doesn't exist. Here's their new image explaining the model line-up:

 So the lineup now, from most to least expensive, is Carbon, Neon, Hydrogen.

 Except Carbon is currently half price, so right now Neon ($3/million input, $15/million output) is the most expensive of the three - then Carbon ($2/$10), then Hydrogen ($1.50/$7.50). I guess this will make more sense when Carbon doubles to $4/$20 on December 1st.

 I ran some pelicans through the three reasoning levels for Neon - low, medium, high.

 I dropped Argon from my Gemini 4 comparison grid - here's the new Gemini 4 lineup, where the Neon pelicans do look better than Hydrogen and worse than Carbon:

 As I've done with several recent models , I also fired the following prompt against Gemini 4 Neon on "extra" effort level in Google Antigravity:

 Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data 

 Here's the result

title: datasette-arrows 0.1a0
summary:
Release: datasette-arrows 0.1a0 

 Datasette 1.0a43 added the ability for plugins to implement streaming export formats. Datasette core supports streaming CSV and TSV - you can export millions of lines of data from a table without needing to load it all into memory, because those two file formats support streaming data in chunks. The register_output_renderer() plugin hook can now be used to implement the same pattern for other formats.

 I've learned never to release a new plugin feature without accompanying it with a plugin that uses it.

 Claude Fable 5.2 suggested the Apache Arrow streaming format as a good option, and built this plugin in almost a single shot.

 Add the plugin to Datasette ( datasette install datasette-arrows ) and the export dialog gains this new Arrow option:

 This screenshot is from Datasette's main branch - the most recent release doesn't yet group streaming formats such as Arrow with the TSV and CSV in the "All rows in this table" section, but that's coming in the next alpha release.

 Tags: datasette , projects

title: [AINews] GPT-6.2 Astra, the #2 Frontier Model is better and 20%-600% cheaper, but has mixed reviews; 6.2 Sol likely main workhorse
summary:
OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol today, two days before Anthropic’s expected first trading day . In Artificial Analysis ’ tests, Sol ties September’s Astra at about 15% of the cost per task . New Astra scores 62 on the Intelligence Index, just behind Fable 5.2 at 65. Net net, Anthropic still owns the world’s best model, but OpenAI owns the world’s most efficient models in terms of intelligence per $. 

 What’s more unusual about this launch is the STRONGLY negative influencer feedback… 

 which prompted a defensive response … 

 View post on X ↗ 

 We think that some of this is overreacting and normal influencer tendency to either have everything be 🤯🤯🤯 or the literal WORST.MODEL.EVER, BUT also that some of the criticisms are valid, and the RL artefacts are noticeable and downright bizarre (don’t even get us started about the terrible launch video ). However, we still use it to automate our work and that’s all that matters in the end. 

 Great ship, but Anthropic’s IPO is unaffected and that will be probably the headline of the week/year/decade (until OpenAI IPO’s….)
